subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured arbitrary-basename workspace files as part of the core `bootstrap-extra-files` hook contract, or keep that hook limited to recognized workspace bootstrap filenames?
rationale: The implementation can be narrow, but it changes which workspace files may enter deterministic system-prompt context and therefore needs a maintainer decision on product scope and guardrails.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files after the linked PR or a replacement preserves workspace guards, budgets, docs, ordering, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Reject arbitrary file injection for this hook and route custom context needs to first-class filename or broader workspace convention proposals.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context API
options.body: Pause this specific hook expansion until maintainers choose a broader workspace discovery or context-file API.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files after the linked PR or a replacement preserves workspace guards, budgets, docs, ordering, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original hook feature and has recent ownership signals in the workspace bootstrap loader path.
